title: Finite affine-cover data and eventual local ample-twist bounds
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $S$ quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $L$ on $X$ and $M$ on $Y$ be invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume that $L|_{f^{-1}(W)}$ is ample for every affine open $W\subseteq Y$, and $M|_{g^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq S$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Put $h=g\circ f$. Then $h$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact, and there exist $r\geq0$ and affine opens $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ covering $S$ with the following properties. For every $i$, set $Y_i=g^{-1}(V_i)$, $X_i=h^{-1}(V_i)=f^{-1}(Y_i)$, let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the restriction of $f$, and put $L_i=L|_{X_i}$ and $M_i=M|_{Y_i}$. The map $f_i$ is of finite type and quasi-compact, $L_i,M_i$ are invertible, $L_i|_{f_i^{-1}(W)}$ is ample for every affine open $W\subseteq Y_i$, and $M_i$ is ample on $Y_i$. There are integers $a_i\geq0$ such that $L_i\otimes f_i^*(M_i^{\otimes a})$ is ample on $X_i$ for every integer $a\geq a_i$. Module pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with zeroth power the structure module. The assertion permits $r=0$ when $S$ is empty.

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $h=g\circ f$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] to the quasi-compact scheme $S$ and enumerate its finite affine cover as $V_1,\ldots,V_r$. If $S$ is empty choose the empty cover; then every assertion indexed by $i$ is vacuous.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and set $Y_i=g^{-1}(V_i)$, $X_i=h^{-1}(V_i)$. The equality $X_i=f^{-1}(Y_i)$ is the identity for inverse images of a composite. The restricted map $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ is the base change of $f$ along $Y_i\hookrightarrow Y$: a pair of maps to $X$ and $Y_i$ agreeing over $Y$ factors uniquely through the open $f^{-1}(Y_i)$. Thus clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $f_i$ finite type, and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] makes it quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), finite affine-cover reduction; Tags 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), and 0892(1) (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample).

proof.text: For each i put U = g^{-1}(V_i). Pullback invertibility in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] makes L_i invertible; the hypothesis on M supplies invertibility and ampleness of M_i. For an affine open W in U, its image W_prime under U -> Y is affine by Mathlib IsAffineOpen.image_of_isOpenImmersion. Apply the hypothesis on L to W_prime. Mathlib image_morphismRestrict_preimage gives the canonical scheme isomorphism j from (f restricted to U)^{-1}(W) to f^{-1}(W_prime), with j followed by the latter inclusion equal to the two nested inclusions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] along j (an affine morphism because it is an isomorphism). The composition comparisons nonempty_tensorPullbackComp of [def-pc-module-pullback], together with this equality of composite inclusions, identify the resulting module with the nested tensor pullback of L. Transport invertibility by IsInvertible.of_iso in [def-sc-invertible-module] and ampleness by [lem-sc-ample-iso]. This proves the required relative ampleness of L_i for every affine W, without any separatedness assumption on U.

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), finite affine-cover reduction; Tags 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), and 0892(1) (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample).

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-relative-ample-absolute-twist] with $(Z,T,f,N,M)=(X_i,Y_i,f_i,L_i,M_i)$. Step 2 supplies quasi-compactness of $f_i$; step 3 supplies invertibility, ampleness of $M_i$, and ampleness of $L_i$ above every affine open of $Y_i$. It gives an integer $a_i\geq0$ such that $L_i\otimes f_i^*(M_i^{\otimes a})$ is ample for every integer $a\geq a_i$. Choosing these bounds for the finitely many indices completes all the stated data.
